model_output.summary: At Cardinal Health, you developed features for an internal inventory application using React and Spring Boot. The projects extend that web development story with a campus ordering app and smaller Python and JavaScript applications. Together with the internship title and degree, they position you for entry-level software engineering. The internship description doesn't name a feature or problem you handled, so a reviewer has little to compare with the project work.
strengths: The inventory application bullet connects React and Spring Boot to a specific business application.
BuckeyeBites names its team setting, technology stack and user-facing functionality, giving the project a recognizable shape.
The finance tracker describes both expense tracking and spending visualization, making the Python work more concrete than a language list alone.
gaps: The inventory application features aren't named, so the internship's technical contribution remains broad.
The unit-test bullet doesn't identify what was tested, leaving the testing work difficult to assess.
The skills list includes technologies such as Docker and Jenkins without examples of their use, making proficiency in them uncertain.
